channel.title: Latest alerts from washingtonpost.com
channel.description: An unofficial feed created by Derek Willis.

item.title: Major League Baseball drops proposal to build a ballpark in Wyoming’s Grand Teton National Park
item.description: League officials had approached the Trump administration about the viability of playing a game at the national park, and a National Park Service official had scouted potential locations. MLB Commissioner Rob Manfred said in a Thursday letter that “it has become clear the local community does not want us to continue evaluating" the park as a potential site.

item.title: Supermarket self-checkouts are a blessing and a curse
item.description: They promised an easier, speedier shopping experience. So why do many of us hate them?

item.title: Trump administration paid for campaign-style ads with millions meant for border security, memorials
item.description: Democrats say the ads break multiple federal laws by using taxpayer money for political purposes that Congress never authorized. The White House defends the ads as public service announcements.

item.title: D.C. and Amazon settle lawsuit over deliveries to majority-Black neighborhoods
item.description: Amazon Prime customers who experienced slower deliveries because they lived in neighborhoods east of the Anacostia River, which are majority-Black, will receive millions of dollars in refunds after the company settled a lawsuit brought by D.C., the city attorney general’s office said Thursday.

item.title: Christa Pike in critical condition after botched Tennessee execution, lawyers say
item.description: An attorney for Pike demanded that Gov. Bill Lee (R) commute her sentence after an attempt to execute her by lethal injection failed.

item.title: Judge says U.S. can’t prosecute ex-Olympian again in Reflecting Pool case
item.description: The case against David Hearn, whom the government accused of vandalism, has been dismissed with prejudice.

item.title: Renée Good’s family sues Trump officials, saying fatal shooting in Minneapolis was ‘not an accident’
item.description: The death of the mother of three sparked protests and scrutiny over how federal officers are using force against both immigrants and protesters.

item.title: Supreme Court agrees to review ICE’s mandatory detention policy for immigrants
item.description: The case is one of the first the Supreme Court has accepted since its summer recess ended, and it promises to be among the most consequential of the term that officially begins next week.

item.title: Treasury releases rules for nation’s first federal school voucher program, set to steer billions of tax dollars to private schools
item.description: The program, called the Federal Scholarship Tax Credit, was created by last year’s giant Republican tax and spending bill. It provides a tax credit for donations to scholarship-granting organizations, which will pass along the money to families.

item.title: Florida county discovers mysterious Flock cameras with no obvious owner
item.description: The discovery presented a mystery about the controversial surveillance technology: Who installed these devices, and who had access to the data they collected?

item.title: Christa Pike survived two doses of lethal injection, prompting Tennessee to halt her execution and begin emergency medical care
item.description: Pike, who was convicted in a brutal 1995 killing, continued to breathe for nearly an hour after she was administered the drugs, her legal team said. Gov. Bill Lee said late Wednesday that he was halting all scheduled executions for the rest of 2026 and ordering a “comprehensive, third-party review to determine exactly what occurred.”

item.title: Supreme Court says Tennessee can move forward with the execution of Christa Pike in 1995 murder
item.description: Pike was scheduled to die Wednesday morning, but the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 6th Circuit imposed a last-minute stay. The Supreme Court’s decision Wednesday evening appears to extinguish the last possible reprieve for Pike, who as an 18-year-old helped carry out a brutal murder of a fellow teen.

item.title: This $60 rye bread is everything that’s right and wrong with New York, food critic Elazar Sontag writes
item.description: In Austria, Martin Auer’s loaves sell for roughly $16. Sontag sampled the spendy NYC version to find out whether the taste matches the price.

item.title: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth details six new initiatives in fiery, partisan address to hundreds of U.S. troops
item.description: The Pentagon chief called for the establishment of a new headquarters focused on drone warfare and touted the recruitment of billionaire tech titans Elon Musk and Palmer Luckey to develop a next generation of weapons.

item.title: The House reimburses lawmakers for D.C. expenses. See who spent the most.
item.description: Taxpayers spent 21 percent more last year on the program, which helps cover the costs of food and lodging in Washington, a Post analysis found.

item.title: Two people were killed in a workplace shooting in Northern Virginia and the suspect is dead, police say
item.description: The suspect, a co-worker, died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound in a standoff with Virginia State Police, authorities said.

item.title: No criminal laws were broken, Federal Reserve watchdog finds in probe of renovation costs that Trump had criticized Powell over
item.description: The Federal Reserve failed to effectively oversee the renovation of its headquarters, letting construction costs more than double without ever locking in a price ceiling, the central bank’s inspector general found in a report.

item.title: Federal Trade Commission launches broad investigation into Anthropic and OpenAI
item.description: The investigation could provide backing for the Trump administration’s position that existing laws are sufficient to hold artificial intelligence companies accountable, as officials seek to resist a push by some in the industry and Congress to establish a new system of regulations for the technology.

item.title: Three people critically wounded in workplace shooting in Northern Virginia; search underway for suspect, police say
item.description: The shooting occurred about 7 a.m. Wednesday at a United Rentals facility in Manassas, authorities said.

item.title: These are the three most chilling words in the Cornell rape case texts, columnist Monica Hesse writes
item.description: “Shop still open?” These three words were reportedly captured in a group chat of members of Cornell University’s Phi Chi fraternity at 1:42 in the morning on Oct. 19, 2024.

item.title: Execution of Tennessee woman on hold after court intervenes hours before she was scheduled to be put to death
item.description: In the lead-up to Christa Pike’s scheduled execution for her role in a 1995 killing, hundreds of legal advocates and trauma experts argued her age at the time of her crime and extensive history of sexual abuse as a child and teen should shape the severity of her punishment.

item.title: Trump can fire Hegseth. He can’t easily undo the damage.
item.description: The Pentagon would have to rebuild expertise, trust and stability if the secretary is forced out.

item.title: U.S. withdraws forces in Iraq as balance of power shifts to Iran
item.description: The last remaining forces relocated to Jordan, the headquarters for the ongoing mission to fight Islamic State militants, U.S. officials said. More than two decades of American involvement in Iran resulted in the deaths of hundreds of thousands of Iraqi civilians and thousands of U.S. troops.

item.title: Pilot on Tel Aviv-bound flight tried to crash plane after cockpit stabbing, Netanyahu says
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he had spoken to an Israeli passenger who, along with a crew member, “managed to force their way into the cockpit, and together they subdued the pilot who had carried out the stabbing as he was trying to sabotage the plane’s systems.”

item.title: The Kennedy Center was solvent when Trump took over. Then its finances collapsed.
item.description: The Post examined 15 years of the institution’s financial records to see why it went south after the president took over.

item.title: Violent clash in cockpit and 18,000-foot nosedive raise terrorism fears as passenger jet headed for Israel makes emergency landing
item.description:
Israeli officials said they were investigating the possibility of a serious security incident or terrorist attack, a person familiar with the matter said.
Israeli news outlets broadcast interviews with passengers describing a violent struggle inside the cockpit and photos of passengers with bloodied shirts.

item.description: Hegseth is expected to announce that the number of top officers will be reduced by as much as 20 percent, officials said.

item.title: Why ‘Let’s go, Brandon’ is worth a legal fight
item.description: The effort to regulate the “profane” political slogan runs up against decades of Supreme Court precedent.

item.title: Supreme Court allows Trump administration, for now, to resume ‘third country’ deportations
item.description: The high court will later hear arguments and make a final ruling on the controversial policy of sending migrants to countries where they are not citizens.

item.title: Former special counsel Jack Smith clashes with senators over Trump investigations, says he will not be silenced
item.description: Smith defended his scrutiny of President Donald Trump’s efforts to overturn the 2020 election and handling of classified documents. Republicans are pressing for a Justice Department inquiry of Smith’s conduct.

item.title: Immigrant shot by ICE officer in Austin is charged with assault
item.description: An unsealed affidavit said the man, Wilber Garcés Pérez, struck a U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer in the torso with his vehicle’s side-view mirror as he fled the scene of a traffic stop Sept. 20. The ICE officer later shot Garcés in the upper back through the back right window of Garcés’s car, the affidavit said.

item.title: Trump launches government chatbot at America.gov, urging a wary public not to fear AI
item.description: Washington’s concerns are at a high after rogue AI agents probed government websites, but the White House has focused on the technology’s promise. Its new chatbot for researching public services was unveiled as part of a day-long event featuring Cabinet members and tech executives.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy is back in court after her murder case ended in a mistrial
item.description: The Massachusetts mother who killed her three children by strangulation in 2023 is appearing before a judge to determine how the case will move forward. The most pressing question is whether the prosecution will seek to retry Clancy.

item.description: No modern president has done more to personally reshape the nation’s capital. It’s an effort that Trump’s deputies and allies credit as a major achievement. Many others just want him to stop.

item.title: Senate passes sweeping bill on college sports to regulate transfer rules, payments to athletes
item.description: The bill would establish national rules governing “name, image and likeness” payments to athletes, revenue sharing, transfers and eligibility. The legislation now heads to the House, where it will likely encounter resistance.

item.title: OpenAI cancels release of its next AI model, citing safety issues
item.description: The artificial intelligence company said the model was found to take actions beyond the instructions it received and did not accurately communicate to human users what it did. The cancellation comes days after OpenAI said it would pause development of new highly capable AI models out of concern that the company doesn’t have appropriate safeguards to keep the technology from behaving in unintended ways.

item.title: Why is Ringo Starr still performing at 86? Because he can.
item.description: The drummer is onstage again, with death-defying energy and feel-good vibes.

item.title: U.S. test scores keep falling. But these states are getting it right.
item.description: A handful of states and the nation’s capital offer a road map to improvement in student learning.

item.title: Trump administration touts savings for car buyers as it rolls back fuel economy standards. Analysts have doubts on price cuts.
item.description: The Trump administration has pitched new rules as a way for people to save money — one potential solution to the affordability debate that has roiled the country in recent years amid high inflation and rising costs — though analysts have expressed skepticism about whether any savings would reach consumers.

item.title: I’m a sports medicine doctor. Here’s what I tell my patients about peptides.
item.description: Peptides may allow physicians to help patients in ways they previously could not, Jordan D. Metzl writes. But not all of these compounds are created equal.
